references.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
references.section: Tower B specialty plumbing fixture standard
references.content:
The following specialty fixtures were specified by the Tower B design team and installed throughout North Campus Tower B:

- **Aqualine SV-200 sensor flush valves** on every patient and staff toilet. The SV-200 uses a proprietary solenoid module and diaphragm kit; there is no generic or cross-manufacturer substitute.
- **Aqualine sensor faucets** at hand hygiene sinks, using a model-specific sensor faucet solenoid.
- **ThermaMix TMV-50 thermostatic mixing valves** controlling hot water delivery temperature at point-of-use and unit-level locations. These valves are part of the Lakeshore water management program for Legionella control.
- **MedGuard MG-4 medical gas zone valve boxes** and MedGuard MG-4 headwall outlets for oxygen, medical air, and vacuum. The O2 outlet latch assembly is model-specific to the MG-4 outlet body.
- **Reduced pressure zone (RPZ) backflow preventers** at domestic water, process water, and equipment connections, serviced with manufacturer RPZ backflow repair kits and relief valve assemblies.

Repair parts for these Tower B fixtures are not stocked by general building supply distributors and are not interchangeable with the commodity parts used in other buildings.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Aqualine SV-200 sensor flush valve components
references.content: The Aqualine SV-200 consists of a chrome valve body, a control stop with integral strainer, a diaphragm kit, a sensor and control module (the "sensor eye"), a sealed solenoid module, a hardwired 24 VAC power supply or battery pack, and a manual override button. The solenoid module is a proprietary sealed assembly specific to the SV-200. **There is no generic or cross-manufacturer substitute for the SV-200 solenoid module**; non-Aqualine solenoids will not mate to the valve body or respond to the sensor control signal, and their use voids the fixture warranty.

references.title: Plumbing Parts Supply and Consignment Agreement - Great Lakes Plumbing Supply (Expired)
references.section: §3 Consignment stock of Tower B specialty parts under the Great Lakes agreement
references.content:
§3.1 Great Lakes maintained **consignment stock** of North Campus Tower B specialty plumbing parts on-site at North Campus, in a locked consignment cage within the Central Plant storeroom. Inventory in the cage remained the property of Great Lakes until withdrawn by Lakeshore.

§3.2 The consignment stock list was jointly set by Great Lakes and the Lakeshore plumbing supervisor and included, at minimum:

- Aqualine SV-200 sensor flush valve solenoid modules, diaphragm kits, and complete assemblies
- Aqualine sensor faucet solenoids
- ThermaMix TMV-50 thermostatic mixing valves and rebuild kits
- MedGuard MG-4 medical gas zone valves, O2 outlet latch assemblies, and vacuum outlet rebuild kits
- RPZ backflow repair kits and relief valve assemblies in sizes used in Tower B

§3.3 Lakeshore technicians withdrew consignment parts as needed, logging each withdrawal against the work order in the computerized maintenance management system (CMMS). Lakeshore was invoiced only upon withdrawal.

§3.4 Great Lakes performed a weekly cycle count and replenished the cage to agreed par levels within two Business Days.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Aqualine SV-200 parts availability and stocking recommendation
references.content: Aqualine recommends that facilities with more than 50 installed SV-200 valves maintain on-site spares of solenoid modules and diaphragm kits equal to at least 5% of the installed base, because these parts are manufactured in batches and distributor stock is limited. Aqualine does not distribute through general building supply channels. A fixture with a failed solenoid module and no spare available must remain out of service until the replacement part arrives.

references.title: Facilities Operations Monthly Review - Minutes, June 2026
references.section: June 2026 discussion of the Tower B plumbing backlog
references.content:
Nolan Achterberg reported a growing plumbing work order backlog in North Campus Tower B since March, primarily sensor flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlet repairs on inpatient units, including the ICUs. Most of the aged Tower B plumbing work orders are on hold in "Awaiting Parts" status for Aqualine SV-200 solenoid modules and MedGuard MG-4 O2 outlet latch assemblies ordered from ACME Mechanical Supply. Several patient rooms have been taken out of service pending parts. Nolan noted that under the prior Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement these parts were pulled from the consignment cage the same day, and that Facilities was not consulted on the Exhibit B specialty item list in the ACME agreement before it was signed.

Tobias Lund (Supply Chain) stated that the ACME delays are **temporary**, attributed to a manufacturer allocation issue at Aqualine and to ACME establishing new manufacturer accounts. Supply Chain expects lead times to normalize by the end of the summer. The first ACME quarterly business review was held in May 2026; Supply Chain reported that fill rate reporting by Exhibit was not yet available from ACME at that time.

Charlotte Engel (Nursing) reported that out-of-service rooms in Tower B are affecting patient flow and ED boarding, and asked for estimated return-to-service dates for each room.

references.title: Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Supply Agreement - ACME Mechanical Supply
references.section: §4 Delivery lead times, consignment, and backorders under the ACME agreement
references.content:
§4.1 **Stocked items.** ACME shall deliver Stocked Items (Exhibit A) to the designated Lakeshore campus receiving dock within two (2) Business Days of order receipt.

§4.2 **Non-stocked specialty items.** For Non-Stocked Specialty Items listed in Exhibit B, ACME shall use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver within ten (10) Business Days of order receipt. Lead times for Exhibit B items are targets and are dependent on manufacturer availability.

§4.3 **No consignment.** No consignment inventory, vendor-managed inventory, or on-site stock is provided under this Agreement. Lakeshore is responsible for any safety stock it elects to purchase and hold.

§4.4 **Backorders.** If any ordered item is backordered, ACME shall notify Lakeshore within two (2) Business Days of order receipt and provide a committed estimated delivery date (ETA). If a backorder exceeds fifteen (15) Business Days from order receipt, Lakeshore may source the item from another supplier and charge ACME the difference between the alternate supplier's price and the Agreement price.

§4.5 **Expedited delivery.** Lakeshore may request expedited delivery of any item at Lakeshore's cost, except as provided in §7.1.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Aqualine SV-200 diaphragm kit replacement procedure
references.content:
Symptoms of a worn or fouled diaphragm include a continuous run-on after flush, short flushes, or a weak flush. To replace the SV-200 diaphragm:

1. Close the control stop and relieve pressure.
2. Remove the top cover and inner cover.
3. Lift out the diaphragm assembly and inspect the bypass orifice.
4. Install the new Aqualine SV-200 diaphragm kit (Aqualine part SV200-DK). Generic flushometer diaphragms are not dimensionally compatible with the SV-200 relief valve seat.
5. Reassemble, open the control stop, and verify flush volume.

references.title: Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Supply Agreement - ACME Mechanical Supply
references.section: §1 Parties and term of the ACME Mechanical Supply agreement
references.content:
§1.1 This Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Supply Agreement, agreement no. LH-SC-2026-017 (the "Agreement"), is entered into between Lakeshore Health ("Lakeshore") and ACME Mechanical Supply ("ACME").

§1.2 The Agreement is effective 2026-02-24 and continues for an initial term of three (3) years, renewing for successive one-year terms unless either party gives ninety (90) days' written notice of non-renewal.

§1.3 ACME is the primary supplier of plumbing repair parts, fixtures, and related mechanical maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) items for all Lakeshore campuses: North Campus, South Campus, and Riverside Campus. This Agreement replaces the prior plumbing parts supply arrangement with Great Lakes Plumbing Supply.

references.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
references.section: Tower B specialty parts supply and storage history
references.content: From the Tower B opening in 2019 until February 2026, specialty repair parts for Tower B fixtures were supplied by Great Lakes Plumbing Supply under a consignment arrangement, with consignment stock held on-site in the North Campus Central Plant storeroom (see Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement LH-SC-2019-044). Effective 2026-02-24, plumbing parts are supplied by ACME Mechanical Supply under agreement LH-SC-2026-017. Supply Chain is the owner of vendor agreements; Facilities Operations is the owner of fixture standards. Technicians should consult the current supply agreement for lead times before committing a repair date to a nursing unit.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Aqualine SV-200 solenoid module replacement procedure
references.content:
1. Close the control stop and press the override to relieve pressure.
2. Disconnect power at the module connector.
3. Remove the top cover using the Aqualine security tool.
4. Unthread the solenoid module from the valve body by hand; do not use pliers on the solenoid housing.
5. Inspect the solenoid port and pilot orifice for debris. Clean with water only.
6. Install the new Aqualine SV-200 solenoid module (Aqualine part SV200-SOL) with the new O-ring supplied.
7. Reconnect power, open the control stop, and verify three consecutive sensor-activated flushes.

references.title: Supply Chain Memo - Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Vendor Consolidation
references.section: Summary of the plumbing parts vendor consolidation decision
references.content: Supply Chain has completed its FY26 review of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) suppliers. As part of the system-wide vendor consolidation initiative, Lakeshore Health will consolidate plumbing and mechanical parts purchasing under a single supplier, ACME Mechanical Supply. The new supply agreement, no. LH-SC-2026-017, takes effect February 24, 2026. The current Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement ends February 23, 2026, and will not be renewed.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: SV-200 sensor indicator light status codes
references.content:
The sensor window contains an indicator LED that communicates status:

| Indicator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Single green blink on approach | Normal; user detected |
| No light | No power (check battery or 24 VAC supply) |
| Slow red blink (1 per 2 s) | Low battery or low supply voltage |
| Rapid red blink, valve does not flush | Solenoid fault or solenoid not responding |
| Continuous red | Sensor obstructed or sensor fault |

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Scope of the Aqualine SV-200 service manual excerpt
references.content: This excerpt covers troubleshooting and repair of the Aqualine SV-200 sensor-operated flush valve as installed on water closets throughout North Campus Tower B at Lakeshore Health. It is intended for licensed plumbers trained on the SV-200. General Maintenance technicians are not authorized to perform SV-200 flushometer or sensor valve repairs under SOP FAC-OPS-014. Refer to the full manufacturer manual for installation and commissioning.

references.section: Exhibit B specialty item classification in the ACME agreement
references.content: Items in the plumbing category were classified as either stocked (Exhibit A) or non-stocked specialty (Exhibit B) by Supply Chain category management, using ACME's stocking catalog and Lakeshore's twelve-month usage history. Exhibit B consists primarily of manufacturer-specific parts for North Campus Tower B fixtures, including Aqualine sensor flush valve components, ThermaMix mixing valves, MedGuard medical gas components, and RPZ backflow repair kits. references.title: Lakeshore Health Campus and Building Facilities Reference
references.section: Commodity plumbing fixtures in other Lakeshore buildings
references.content: All Lakeshore buildings other than Tower B use standard commodity plumbing fixtures: manual or standard-diaphragm flushometers, conventional two-handle or single-lever faucets with generic cartridges, and standard medical gas outlets from multiple manufacturers installed during various renovations. Parts for these fixtures are carried in campus shop stock and are available from most plumbing distributors, typically same-day or next-day. Tower A (1972) and Riverside Hospital (1965) have the oldest piping systems and the highest rate of leak and drain work orders, but their parts are commodity items.

references.title: Aqualine SV-200 Sensor Flush Valve Service Manual (Excerpt)
references.section: Troubleshooting a red blinking SV-200 sensor flush valve
references.content:
When an SV-200 sensor flush valve shows a red blinking indicator and does not flush:

1. Verify the area is safe and the fixture is not overflowing. Close the control stop if water is running continuously.
2. Clean the sensor window with a soft damp cloth. Remove any tape, labels, or obstructions.
3. Check supply voltage at the module connector (24 VAC nominal) or replace batteries on battery models. A slow red blink that clears after battery replacement indicates a power issue only.
4. Press the manual override button. If the valve flushes with the override but not with the sensor, the sensor module is likely faulty. If the valve does not flush with the override, proceed to solenoid diagnosis.
5. A rapid red blink that persists after power is confirmed indicates a solenoid fault. Replace the solenoid module per the procedure below.

references.title: Supply Chain Memo - Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Vendor Consolidation
references.section: Expected service level impact of the ACME Mechanical Supply transition
references.content: ACME will deliver stocked items within two business days to any campus receiving dock. Specialty items not carried in ACME's regional inventory will be ordered from the manufacturer with a ten business day lead time target. ACME has committed to a 95% monthly fill rate, with remedies available to Lakeshore if that level is not met. Supply Chain has reviewed ACME's delivery performance with two peer health systems in the region. **No material impact on service levels is expected** as a result of this transition.

references.title: Plumbing and Mechanical Parts Supply Agreement - ACME Mechanical Supply

references.section: §7 Service levels, reporting, and remedies under the ACME agreement

It does not replace building-specific as-built drawings, which are maintained in the Facilities document management system.

references.section: Expected cost savings from the ACME Mechanical Supply consolidation
references.content: Based on twelve months of purchase history, ACME pricing represents approximately 11% unit cost savings across the plumbing parts category. Additional savings are expected from reduced invoice volume, elimination of the consignment carrying charge embedded in Great Lakes pricing, and consolidated freight. Savings will be reported in the monthly Supply Chain value analysis report.

references.title: Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) for Construction, Renovation, and Maintenance
references.section: Scope of the ICRA policy for plumbing and maintenance work
references.content: IC-210 applies to all Facilities Operations staff, contractors, and vendors performing work in Lakeshore buildings. Routine plumbing work that does not disturb walls, ceilings, or floors (for example, replacing a faucet cartridge, rebuilding an exposed flush valve, or replacing a headwall outlet component without opening the wall) does not require an ICRA permit. **Plumbing work in patient care areas that requires wall or ceiling penetration requires an ICRA permit** before work begins. This includes opening a chase wall to access a concealed flush valve or supply, removing ceiling tiles above an occupied patient care area, and cutting into a headwall.

references.title: Work Order Priority and Response Policy
references.section: Purpose and scope of the work order priority policy FAC-POL-002
references.content: This policy establishes the priority levels used for all Facilities Operations corrective maintenance work orders at Lakeshore Health, and the response and completion time targets associated with each priority. It applies to all campuses and buildings and to all trades: plumbing, electrical, HVAC, carpentry, and General Maintenance. Priority is assigned by the Facilities service desk at intake and may be changed by the responding technician or supervisor based on field conditions.

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: Utility systems management plan expectations at Lakeshore
references.content: Lakeshore is expected to maintain a written utility management plan that identifies the utility systems that support patient care (electrical distribution and emergency power, HVAC, domestic water, medical gas and vacuum, plumbing and drainage, steam, and communications), inventories the critical components of each, and assigns maintenance, inspection, and testing activities and frequencies. Surveyors typically review the inventory, the maintenance strategy chosen for each component, and evidence that planned activities were completed on time. At Lakeshore, the utility inventory and activity schedule are held in the CMMS, and completion is reported monthly to the Environment of Care Committee.

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: About this Lakeshore internal regulatory summary
references.content: This document is Lakeshore Health's internal summary, written in our own words, of what our accreditation surveyors generally look for in the Environment of Care (EC) chapter as it applies to utility systems. It is not a copy of any accreditation standard and does not replace the current published standards, which Accreditation and Regulatory Readiness maintains under license. Facilities Operations, Plant Operations, and Infection Prevention should use this summary to prepare for tracer activity and to understand how Lakeshore procedures support compliance.

references.section: September 2026 after-hours General Maintenance plumbing callbacks
references.content:
Wendell Ruiz reported that overnight General Maintenance callouts for plumbing issues have continued to rise each month since April. Most are P2 Urgent calls for toilets and flush valves, mixing valves, and medical gas outlets on Tower B inpatient units. Under SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4, these calls route to the GM on-call first; GM technicians are not licensed for flushometer or sensor valve, medical gas, or backflow repair, so they make the area safe and the ticket is reassigned to a plumber at the start of the next day shift. Charge nurses have reported repeated overnight visits to the same room without repair. Charlotte Engel noted that Nursing understood from prior practice (Rev 3) that P2 plumbing calls would page the on-call plumber.

Action item AI-2026-06-04 (review effect of SOP FAC-OPS-014 Rev 4 on after-hours plumbing response and completion times) remains **open**. references.section: §4 Pricing and invoicing under the Great Lakes Plumbing Supply agreement

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: Water management program for Legionella and hot water temperature control
references.content: Lakeshore is expected to maintain a water management program that identifies areas of the water system where Legionella and other waterborne pathogens could grow and spread, establishes control measures, and monitors them. Key control measures include maintaining hot water temperatures high enough in storage and distribution to limit bacterial growth, while protecting patients from scalding at the point of use. At Lakeshore, this balance is achieved with thermostatic mixing valves, including the ThermaMix TMV-50 valves installed in North Campus Tower B, which blend hot and cold water to a safe delivery temperature. Failed mixing valves must be corrected promptly because they can produce either scald-risk temperatures or lukewarm water that supports bacterial growth. The program also covers flushing of low-use outlets, backflow prevention, and response to out-of-range test results. The Water Management Team, co-chaired by Plant Operations and Infection Prevention, reviews monitoring data quarterly.

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: Documentation of utility system failures and disruptions
references.content: Hospitals are expected to have procedures for responding to utility system disruptions, including who to notify, how to obtain emergency repair services, and what clinical interventions to take when a utility fails (for example, portable oxygen or suction). Surveyors expect utility failures to be documented, investigated, and reported to the Environment of Care Committee, with corrective actions tracked to completion. Lakeshore documents utility failures in the utility failure log and in the CMMS work order. Patterns of repeated failures or prolonged repair times for the same system are expected to be analyzed and addressed through the performance improvement process.

references.title: Facilities Operations Monthly Review - Minutes, June 2026
references.section: June 2026 review of work order key performance indicators
references.content: Glen Harlow presented May work order performance. Overall system volume was in line with seasonal expectations, with North Campus continuing to carry the highest volume of any campus. P3 and P4 completion compliance remained at target. P1 response compliance was at target for all trades. The plumbing trade showed declining P2 completion compliance, concentrated at North Campus. The CMMS dashboard has been updated to show time in "Awaiting Parts" status by trade and building.

references.title: MedGuard MG-4 Zone Valve Box and Station Outlet Maintenance (Excerpt)
references.section: Lakeshore qualified personnel rule for MedGuard MG-4 medical gas work
references.content: Under Lakeshore's internal medical gas rule, which follows nationally recognized medical gas installation practice, **only licensed medical gas installers** credentialed by Lakeshore may open an MG-4 zone valve box, operate a zone valve except in an emergency shutoff, or disassemble or repair a station outlet. General Maintenance technicians are not licensed for medical gas work under SOP FAC-OPS-014 and may not perform these tasks. After any repair that opens the system, the affected zone must be verified for cross-connection, pressure, flow, and purity before return to service, and the verification documented in the CMMS.

references.title: Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) for Construction, Renovation, and Maintenance
references.section: Purpose of the Lakeshore ICRA policy IC-210
references.content: This policy defines when an Infection Control Risk Assessment (ICRA) and ICRA permit are required before construction, renovation, or maintenance work in Lakeshore Health facilities, and the precautions that must be in place. The intent is to protect patients, particularly immunocompromised patients, from airborne and waterborne organisms such as Aspergillus and Legionella that can be released by dust, debris, or disturbed water systems.

references.title: After-Hours Facilities Work Order Dispatch
references.section: Purpose of the after-hours dispatch SOP FAC-OPS-014
references.content: This standard operating procedure defines how Facilities Operations work orders received after hours are routed, triaged, and assigned at all Lakeshore Health campuses (North Campus, South Campus, and Riverside Campus). It applies to work orders entered through the Facilities service desk phone line, the online request portal, and nurse station requests. Priority definitions referenced in this SOP are those in the Work Order Priority and Response Policy, FAC-POL-002.

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: Backflow prevention device testing expectations
references.content: Backflow prevention devices, including reduced pressure zone (RPZ) assemblies, protect the potable water supply from contamination. Surveyors may ask for evidence of annual testing by a certified tester and timely repair of failed devices. Lakeshore performs annual RPZ testing as P4 Scheduled work and treats a failed test as P2 Urgent under FAC-POL-002. Only certified backflow technicians may repair and retest an RPZ device.

references.title: Internal Summary - Joint Commission Environment of Care Expectations for Utility Systems
references.section: Survey readiness actions for Lakeshore utility systems
references.content:
1. Confirm the utility component inventory is current, including Tower B specialty components.
2. Verify medical gas zone valve labeling and accessibility on all inpatient floors.
3. Confirm mixing valve temperature monitoring records for the water management program.
4. Confirm annual backflow test records and closure of failed-test work orders.
5. Review the utility failure log for trends and open corrective actions.

references.title: MedGuard MG-4 Zone Valve Box and Station Outlet Maintenance (Excerpt)
references.section: MedGuard MG-4 spare parts recommendation
references.content: MedGuard recommends that hospitals maintain on-site spares of zone valves for each gas and pipe size in use, O2 outlet latch assemblies, and vacuum rebuild kits, because MG-4 parts are distributed only through authorized medical gas distributors and an outlet awaiting parts results in the patient bed position being unusable.

references.title: MedGuard MG-4 Zone Valve Box and Station Outlet Maintenance (Excerpt)
references.section: MedGuard MG-4 zone valve replacement
references.content: A failed MG-4 zone valve (failure to close fully, stem leakage, or failed gauge port) is replaced as a complete valve assembly (MedGuard part MG4-ZV). MG-4 zone valves are specific to the MG-4 box mounting rail and extension tube dimensions; other manufacturers' zone valves will not fit the MG-4 box without box replacement, which requires wall penetration and an ICRA permit under IC-210.

args.to: ACME Mechanical Supply - Account Manager, with Lakeshore Supply Chain Contract Administration
args.subject: Corrective action required: Tower B Aqualine backorders and Exhibit B fill-rate failures
args.body:
Please review the attached Tower B plumbing work-order evidence and the ACME agreement LH-SC-2026-017. Since March 2026, North Campus Tower B patient-room bathroom repairs using ACME-supplied Aqualine parts have averaged 17.08 days to close and 15.15 days waiting on parts across 46 ACME orders. The delays are concentrated in Aqualine SV-200 flush valve and Aqualine sensor faucet components, with repeated notes of backorders, no ETA, and pushed ETAs.

Representative examples:
- WO-2026-009732: AQL-SV200-DK ordered 2026-07-20; ACME confirmed backorder/no ETA; room taken out of service; received 2026-08-10; closed after 24.2 days.
- WO-2026-009189: AQL-SF-SOL ordered 2026-06-29; ACME confirmed backorder/no ETA and ETA pushed; received 2026-07-20; closed after 23.4 days.
- WO-2026-009161: AQL-SV200-CMP ordered 2026-06-26; room taken out of service; ACME backorder/no ETA; received 2026-07-16; closed after 20.4 days.

Under LH-SC-2026-017, these Aqualine parts are Exhibit B Non-Stocked Specialty Items, but ACME must provide backorder notice within two business days with a committed ETA, monthly service reporting, and maintain at least 95% monthly fill rate. Facilities meeting minutes report Exhibit B fill rate of 71% in July and 68% in August 2026, triggering the two-consecutive-month remedy.

Please provide a written corrective action plan within ten business days and start shipping subsequent Exhibit B Tower B Aqualine orders by expedited freight at ACME cost until the fill rate is restored. Also provide committed ETAs for all open Tower B Aqualine backorders and support an interim safety-stock plan for AQL-SV200-DK, AQL-SV200-CMP/AQL-SV200-SOL, and AQL-SF-SOL.
